chosen_line.card: All Streams Flow to the Sea

q1_what_did_you_play: All Streams Flow to the Sea at Nibbit first, then Twin Tides taking the Spend 6 Charge half for 12 Block. Order was the whole point: All Streams reads Charge when it resolves, so it has to land while Charge is still 8 and it is printed at 9. If I had led with Twin Tides, Charge would be 2 and the attack would shrink. That sequencing turns 2 energy into 9 damage plus exactly enough Block to eat the telegraphed 12 with nothing spilling over — Nibbit to 25, me at 48 untouched.
q2_other_line_considered: Two, seriously. First, Water's Edge plus All Streams Flow to the Sea for 15 damage, taking the full 12 to the face and dropping to 36. Trading 12 HP for 6 extra damage against an enemy still at 34 is a bad rate this early in the fight, so it lost. Second, Gyorin Formation alone: 10 Block now and 6 more at the start of next turn, which is 16 Block across two turns for 2 energy versus Twin Tides' 12. But it leaks 2 damage this turn and deals nothing, and its 10 is also charge-inflated, so it is buying next turn's defense at the price of this turn's tempo. Twin Tides plus an attack beat it on both axes that mattered.
q3_what_it_gave_up: Charge, mainly. I burned 8 down to 2, which deflates All Streams Flow to the Sea and Gyorin Formation for the next few turns until it rebuilds — a copy of All Streams drawn next turn is a much smaller card than the one I just played. I also gave up the 6 Block that Gyorin would have deposited at the start of my next turn, so I enter that turn naked, and I gave up the 6 damage Water's Edge would have added, along with its Hydro application.
q4_different_intent: Yes. The 12 is what made Twin Tides' expensive half worth the Charge — it is the exact number that makes 12 Block a full negation rather than an overpay. If Nibbit had telegraphed a small hit, a block, a buff, or anything non-damaging, I would have played Water's Edge and All Streams Flow to the Sea for 15 damage and kept all 8 Charge, since there would be nothing to defend against and Charge is worth more banked. If the intent had been much larger than 12, say 20-plus, Twin Tides would stop being a clean negation and I would have looked hard at Gyorin Formation instead, or just accepted the hit and pushed damage.
